title: Planar STL boundary extraction and Gmsh 2D generation
overview: Reads one planar STL body loop, reconstructs its boundary, and generates either a directly bounded planar region or an external-flow fluid domain with the STL body as a wall hole and named outer boundary groups.
principle: STL facets carry coordinates and triangle topology, not standard CFD boundary-condition semantics. Singly incident triangle edges reconstruct the body loop. A sidecar either assigns names to a planar region boundary or defines a rectangular external-flow domain whose four sides are Inlet, Outlet, Symmetry and Farfield and whose internal STL loop is Wall. Physical names require a separate mapping to OneFLOW BC semantics.
architecture: ASCII/Binary STL -> vertex welding and XY topology validation -> single closed body loop -> explicit sidecar domain bounds and outer boundary names -> Gmsh geometry with an internal Wall hole and Fluid surface -> optional Gmsh CLI -> MSH -> existing Gmsh import and CGNS conversion path.

proves: ASCII and binary STL triangle records can be read and a planar square fixture yields one four-edge boundary loop.
The planar STL loop can be used as an internal wall hole inside an explicitly bounded rectangular fluid domain.
The four outer rectangle sides and internal wall are emitted as separate named Gmsh Physical Curve groups.
does_not_prove: Generated outer-flow meshes have been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.
Generated MSH has been converted through CGNS into a OneFLOW native grid.
Boundary names are automatically translated into OneFLOW solver boundary-condition types.
Arbitrary plane orientations, holes, multiple components, curved reconstruction or general multi-cell meshing are supported.
